Definition: Rejecting a distinction because no sharp line marks it. Vague boundaries do not erase real differences; clear cases still differ.
Example: Someone argues, 'There's no exact moment day becomes night, so day and night don't differ.'
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'No sharp line marks when doubt becomes unbelief, so doubt and unbelief are identical.'
HowToRespond: Use clear cases: "Vague boundaries don't erase real differences — let's use clear cases."
